analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy (10 November 2026)
key_insights: Risk assets rallied broadly: S&P 500 closed +2.35% at 7550, its strongest day since the April Iran ceasefire announcement, and is down only 0.25% over the four business days since the midterms. VIX fell 5.72pts to 19.92, the sharpest daily drop since April 2025.

Easing AI-growth fears drove the Philly semiconductor index +6.85% on the day, its best daily gain since July, and +11.35% over two sessions. That unwound almost two thirds of its 15% decline after the midterm results.

DB equity strategists said positioning had become sizeably underweight after last week's moves, and tech positioning was below its post-Liberation Day lows, so conditions were in place for a sharp recovery. There was no obvious catalyst.

Nvidia fell 4.27% to a 7-month low, the only Philly semiconductor index member to decline, after announcing an independent investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang. CoreWeave reports after the US close on Nov 10.

Brent fell 5.85% to a 2-month low of $92.57/bbl and was down another 1.21% to $91.45/bbl in the morning, on hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic deal. A Qatari official told Bloomberg both sides were talking with mediators on deal details.

Trump said it was 'highly unlikely' he would order extensive strikes on Iran, conditional on a 'very strong agreement'. He also posted of 'positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict' while saying the US was 'locked and loaded' if things change.

Tech strength plus lower oil reversed the stagflation playbook. The 2yr Treasury yield rose 5.0bps to 4.56% on an 11.2bps rise in the real yield while the breakeven fell 6.2bps. The 1yr inflation swap fell 13.6bps to below 2% for the first time since mid-August.
Market pricing for a December Fed hike rose from 78% on Friday to 84% at the close. The 10yr rose 2.6bps to 4.88% and the 30yr rose 1.4bps.

October CPI is due today and is the last CPI before the December Fed decision. DB economists expect +0.20% m/m for both headline and core, against a September headline print of +0.65% (fastest in six months). Consensus in the table is +0.30%. There will be no y/y figure because the October 2025 CPI was not produced during last year's government shutdown.
Markets will read CPI through to PCE, but more PCE components only come with Friday's PPI release.
Asia rallied again: KOSPI +4.73% after three straight declines, Nikkei 225 +2.82%, TOPIX +2.06%, TAIEX +2.31%, ASX 200 +1.10%. S&P 500 futures were +0.21% and Nasdaq 100 futures +0.08%.

Europe rose: STOXX 600 +1.26%, DAX +1.73%, FTSE 100 +1.02%, CAC 40 +1.16% (two-month high), FTSE MIB +2.69% (best since April). The Franco-German 10yr spread tightened 3.4bps to a 3-week low of 147bps. 10yr OATs fell 2.3bps and BTPs 2.7bps while the Bund rose 0.9bps to 3.26%.

NY Fed survey: 1yr inflation expectations rose 1bp to 3.91%, the highest since May 2023, and 3yr rose 4bps to 3.29%, the highest since June. The mean probability of higher unemployment in a year rose to 45.3%, the highest since April 2020.
Fed speakers today: Waller, Logan, Schmid, Bowman and Paulson. ECB and BoE speakers are also scheduled. NFIB small business optimism for October is also due.

tension_points.bull_case: AI growth fears eased, the Philly semiconductor index is up 11.35% in two sessions, the VIX fell to 19.92 and oil dropped on US-Iran diplomacy hopes, reversing the stagflation playbook.
tension_points.bear_case: NY Fed 1yr inflation expectations are at 3.91%, the highest since May 2023, and the market prices an 84% chance of a December Fed hike. Expectations of higher unemployment are at the highest since April 2020.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hotter-than-expected October CPI today, ahead of the Fed's December decision, or a breakdown in US-Iran diplomacy, given the US is 'locked and loaded'.
